assessed.reason: In `pytest_runtest_makereport`, the `elif item.config.option.runxfail: pass` branch short-circuits before the skip-location handling, so an unconditional skip reports the location inside skipping.py; the fix is to let skip-mark reports through that branch, plus a changelog entry and a regression test.

The fix is removing `follow_symlinks=False` from the directory check in `visit()` at src/_pytest/pathlib.py:561, plus a regression test and changelog entry; it affects only which directories are walked during collection.
caplog.set_level records the original logger level but never restores the handler level, so the level leaks into later tests; the fix is a small change in src/_pytest/logging.py.

unique_path() in src/_pytest/pathlib.py applies normcase on Windows, lowercasing the conftest path so the derived package name ('python') no longer matches the real folder; the fix is to keep the original case for import while still deduplicating paths, plus a regression test. Estimate is from reading the source only, not verified by running it.

The xdist path serializes only the last reprtraceback and reprcrash in BaseReport._to_json (src/_pytest/reports.py:154-190), so the change is to serialize the full ExceptionChainRepr chain and rebuild it in _from_json (lines 205-255), plus tests and a changelog entry.

_store_type_annotation_node only records bare Name annotations and names inside Subscripts, so an Attribute annotation like abc.ABC is skipped and import abc is wrongly flagged; the fix is a small branch in variables.py plus a regression test (unverified, not run).
The fix is a short guard in pylint/checkers/similar.py (skip similarity computation when min_lines is 0), plus a test and a changelog fragment; no money, auth, or stored-data impact.

The short -v flag takes the generic argparse path, which expects a value, while the long --verbose flag is preprocessed in pylint/config/utils.py. Making -v behave as a flag is a few lines plus a regression test.

The bug is in `_regexp_csv_transfomer` (pylint/config/argument.py:114), which splits on every comma before compiling, so the change is a regex-aware splitter (ignoring commas inside braces, brackets, or escapes) plus a test and changelog fragment; no calculation, auth, or stored data is touched.

The bug is that LogCaptureHandler.reset() (src/_pytest/logging.py:345) rebinds self.records to a new list instead of clearing it in place, so the list that caplog.get_records() holds (set at line 699) drifts apart; changing that to an in-place clear plus a regression test is a one-line fix.
The fix is likely a localized change in how unittest.py handles class-level skips under --pdb, plus a regression test and changelog entry, though I did not open the code to confirm this.

Marks on classes are read through a single `pytestmark` attribute, so a class with two marked bases only keeps the MRO-first list; the fix is a localized change to how `get_unpacked_marks` or `store_mark` merges inherited marks, plus a regression test and changelog entry.

The bug is one expression in num_mock_patch_args (src/_pytest/compat.py:71), where `p.new in sentinels` uses `==` and triggers numpy's ambiguous truth value; switching it to an identity check (`is`) for each sentinel is a one-line fix, plus a regression test and changelog entry.

The fix is a one-line change of the hard-coded lexer from "python3" to "text" in the bpaste submission data (src/_pytest/pastebin.py line 82), plus possibly updating a test that asserts the lexer value.
pytest_collect_file in src/_pytest/python.py matches __init__.py as a test module, so a guard restricting that match to real test packages, plus a regression test, should be a small change.

The bad .replace(".[", "[") is a single line in src/_pytest/python.py, so the code change is one line plus a regression test and a changelog entry; the main effort is verifying that removing it doesn't break other tests.

The bug is a single line at src/_pytest/setuponly.py:69 that formats cached_param with str() (implicit via "{}".format), which triggers BytesWarning under -bb; switching it to saferepr or similar is a one-line change, with no calculation, auth, or stored-data impact.

The fix is probably a small guard in the unittest integration so that, under --pdb, tearDown is skipped for skipped tests the same way it is without --pdb, plus a regression test and changelog entry; I did not open the files to confirm this.

The crash comes from `ast.Name(ident.value, ...)` at expression.py:164 building a Name node for identifiers "None", "True" or "False", which CPython's debug build asserts against; the fix is to emit `ast.NameConstant` for those three words (a few lines plus a test), and I changed nothing.
